title: Missed audit entries during SSO proxy scaling and backpressure event
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a platform autoscaler bounce on 2025-02-09 the SSO proxy experienced transient request-queue backpressure that caused the audit-forwarding agent to drop ~4.3k audit events for a 4 minute window. Root cause analysis shows a combination of (1) a race between the proxy draining and the audit sink connection tear-down, (2) an audit-buffer TTL of 30s that expired before retry attempts, and (3) missing backpressure signals from the audit sink which led the autoscaler to assume healthy throughput. Impact: partial incompleteness in the compliance audit trail for affected customer orgs in the us-east-1 region; potential regulatory exposure for customers with strict retention SLAs.
timeline: 2025-02-09 02:17 UTC - Autoscaler triggered rolling bounce for sso-proxy pool (routine deploy).
2025-02-09 02:18 UTC - SSO proxy pods began termination; inflight requests were drained but audit-forwarder connections were closed prematurely by the sink during an internal GC window.
2025-02-09 02:19 UTC - Observability alert fired: audit-forwarder retry error rate spike (pager to infra-oncall).
2025-02-09 02:20 UTC - Oncall investigated: stack traces showed audit-forwarder dropped events when buffer TTL expired; sink returned 503 intermittently due to a competing maintenance job.

2025-02-09 02:21 UTC - Incident declared. Immediate mitigation: disabled concurrent maintenance job on audit sink and increased forwarder buffer TTL to 5m as a stopgap, restarted sso-proxy with graceful-drain=180s.
2025-02-09 03:00 UTC - Incident resolved for production traffic; post-incident data collection began.
2025-02-10 - Postmortem draft created and initial action items proposed.
2025-02-24 - Compliance team requested formal remediation plan and timeline.
2025-03-01 - This ticket opened to track engineering action items and verification steps.
detected_by: Observability alert: audit-forwarder.retry-error-rate > 10% for 1m (alert ID OBS-AUD-1128)
root_causes: Race during pod termination where audit-forwarder shutdown path closed connections before buffered events were flushed.
Audit sink returned transient 503s during a maintenance task leading to increased retries and eventual buffer TTL expiry.
Autoscaler health probe only measured request success on proxy, not audit-forwarder backlog, so it bounced pods while drain was incomplete.
Lack of end-to-end test coverage for proxy+forwarder drain behavior under concurrent sink maintenance.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Short-term fix: increase forwarder buffer TTL (to 5m) and extend graceful-drain window to 180s. Tradeoff: increased memory for forwarder on bursty nodes until long-term fix is in place.
Long-term: add explicit backpressure / health endpoint from audit sink to autoscaler. Tradeoff: requires changes across infra and possible rollout coordination with compliance team.

We chose to implement a replay/backfill tool instead of attempting aggressive retroactive reconstruction from proxies because request logs are scrubbed and backfill from existing observations is more auditable and verifiable for compliance.
action_items: Luca Romero - Implement connection-safe drain protocol in sso-proxy that waits for audit-forwarder ack or a configurable timeout (due 2025-03-05).
Priya Singh - Extend audit-forwarder buffer TTL and expose buffered-count metric; deploy to canary (due 2025-03-03).
Infra Team (oncall) - Add health endpoint 'audit_sanity' on audit sink returning backlog-aware status that autoscaler will use (due 2025-03-12).
Eng QA - Add end-to-end integration test that simulates sink 503s during proxy drain to catch regressions (due 2025-03-07).
Compliance & Legal - Review backfill approach and approve acceptance criteria for reconstructed events (owner: Maya Chen, due 2025-03-04).

SRE - Build backfill utility that rehydrates missing audit events from request traces and Kinesis raw ingest; produce checksumed artifacts for compliance review (owner: Diego Alvarez, due 2025-03-17).
Docs - Update runbook and oncall checklist for SSO proxy to include audit-forwarder verification steps (owner: Nora Kim, due 2025-03-01).
progress_updates: 2025-02-11 - Mitigation applied: buffer TTL increased in prod to 5m and graceful-drain extended; observed no further drops in retrospective sampling.
2025-02-18 - Canary rollout of extended TTL completed for us-east-1 with no regressions; metrics dashboard added (dashboards.redwood.internal/#/d/abcd-audit-forwarder).
2025-02-24 - Draft design PR opened for drain-protocol: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sso-proxy/pull/2246 (design notes included).
2025-02-28 - Backfill design reviewed by Compliance; outstanding question around event fidelity answered — proceed with reconstruct+annotate approach.
2025-03-01 - This ticket converted from Postmortem->Engineering work; action items assigned.
review_feedback: Maya Chen (Compliance) 2025-02-20: Agreed to TTL short-term but requested formal verification before closing incident. Need signed acceptance for backfill artifacts.
Sanjay Rao (Platform Lead) 2025-02-22: Recommend autoscaler change be gated behind a feature flag and rolled out to dedicated clusters first.

Devin Park (Security) 2025-02-25: Flagged that any backfill must include complete provenance headers and must not attempt to synthesize user IPs—okayed reconstructing event payloads only from existing authenticated request traces.
Design (Nora Kim) 2025-02-26: Suggested adding a visible audit-forwarder backlog indicator in the Console to help customers debug missed events.
verification_plan: Canary: deploy drain-protocol and TTL changes behind feature flag to staging and a single canary cluster for 72h. Monitor 'audit_forwarder.dropped_events' and 'audit_forwarder.buffered_count'.
Load test: run synthetic deploys that trigger drain while sink returns 503s; verify no dropped events for 99.9% of requests.
Compliance signoff: produce backfill artifacts and checksums; Compliance to confirm acceptance criteria before closing ticket.
Post-deploy: run weekly regression check that simulates maintenance job overlap for 30 days.
closure_criteria: All action items completed and merged to main.
Canary and prod verification show dropped events < 0.01% under simulated maintenance conditions.
Compliance signoff on backfill tooling and artifacts documented in Confluence.
Runbook updated and Console backlog indicator shipped or triaged into next cycle.
notes: Do not attempt to derive IP or identity fields for reconstructed events; use existing authenticated trace references to satisfy provenance checks.
This incident highlights that any subsystem that forwards compliance signals must be part of autoscaler's health contract; add to platform architecture checklist.
